question: Should OpenClaw accept this grouped Claw update and partial-recovery contract as the mutation stage of the still-open Claws RFC?
rationale: Tests can validate mechanics, but only maintainers can accept the durable CLI consent model, cross-owner rollback limits, persisted provenance, and operator recovery obligations.

options.title: Accept after live proof
options.body: Keep the current consent and partial-state contract, require inspectable package, cron, and recovery evidence, then land it after its stack dependencies.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Defer package replacement or Gateway cron mutation so the initial update capability has a smaller recovery and upgrade burden.

options.title: Continue RFC incubation
options.body: Keep the PR open without landing until the RFC settles the lifecycle and recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Accept after live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the current consent and partial-state contract, require inspectable package, cron, and recovery evidence, then land it after its stack dependencies.

likelyOwner.reason: The RFC history makes this person the strongest visible product-model decision owner for the agent-centric Claws contract.
